newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Money climbs after good drill results.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Money climbs after good drill results.

text.p: The shares of minerals explorer, Money Moning NL rose sharply on big turnover on Monday after the company reported promising drilling results from its Granny Venn gold prospect, near the town of Menzies in Western Australia.
At 3.20 p.m. (0420 GMT), Money shares were 2.5 cents higher at 25 cents on turnover of 5.0 million shares, representing about 8.9 percent of Money's issued capital.
A Perth-based dealer said the Granny Venn report was most likely reason for the stock's rise.
Money said the drill results continued to give encouragement towards an economic resource.
The company reported significant intercepts from eight holes including seven metres at 16.76 grams per tonne (g/t) gold and 20 metres at 5.39 g/t gold.
"There is also a rumour that Eagle Mining NL has been buying shares," the dealer said.
Eagle acquired a 17.9 percent stake in Money earlier this year when it sold its 20 percent interest in the Dingo Range minerals joint venture in Western Australia's Yandal greenstone belt to Money.
Under Australian law, Eagle cannot buy more than 20 percent of Money's issued capital without launching a takeover offer for the company.
"To my knowledge we have not bought any Money shares today," a spokesman from Eagle said.
At 3.20 p.m. (0420 GMT), Eagle shares were three cents weaker at A$3.00.
